_comment: Task flow for the Codex tool-surface arms. Multi-step with context carried across steps, because the fixed schema cost is paid per request and only compounds over a session. A single-question flow understates it and is not what the r/codex benchmark measured.

target_repo._comment: Pin an exact commit before publishing any number. Indexing whatever main points at today measures a different corpus. Any mid-size repo works; FastAPI is here because benchmarks/results.md already uses it, so corpus characteristics are documented.

steps: Which module defines the dependency injection resolution logic, and what is the entry point function?
Trace how a path operation's dependencies get resolved at request time. Name the functions in call order.
What happens if two dependencies in the same request declare the same sub-dependency? Point at the code that decides.
Where is the response model applied to the return value, and what does it do when the returned object has extra fields?
If I changed the signature of the dependency cache key, what else would need to change? List the files.
Summarize what you learned about this codebase's request lifecycle in under 200 words.
_step_notes: Steps are read-only comprehension tasks with increasing dependence on earlier context. No edits, so every arm runs under sandbox=read-only and no arm can perturb the tree for another. Deliberately answerable without running the code, so a lane that cannot execute is not penalised.
